title: The 10 Best Pneumatic Finish Nailers
subtitle: 15- and 16-gauge air finish nailers for baseboard, casing, crown and cabinets, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A finish nailer drives 15- or 16-gauge nails up to 2-1/2 inches, long enough to hold door casing, baseboard and crown into framing, where an 18-gauge brad nailer is too light. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (switchable sequential and bump fire, a 5-year-plus warranty, a weight under 4.5 lbs and a carrying case). 16-gauge nailers use straight strips; 15-gauge angled nailers hold heavier nails and reach into corners. They run from about $48 for 3PLUS's 16-gauge to $204 for BOSTITCH's 15-gauge kit. Each needs an air compressor.

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: Metabo HPT 16 Gauge Finish Nailer, Lightweight 1-2.5in, NT65M2S
products.verdict: The best-selling finish nailer here: a 3.7 lb 16-gauge with a sequential/bump switch, tool-free depth, a no-mar tip and case, and a 5-year warranty. Builder and Developer magazine has named it its Pro Preferred nailer 12 years running.
products.best_for: Baseboard, casing and most trim work.
products.skip_if: You're hanging heavy crown or jambs; a 15-gauge angled nailer holds better.

products.name: Metabo HPT 15 Gauge Angled Finish Nailer, Selective Actuation, NT65MA4
products.verdict: The most-reviewed finish nailer here: a 15-gauge angled nailer for crown, door and window casing and chair rail, with an angled magazine that reaches into corners, a 360° exhaust and a 5-year warranty.
products.best_for: Crown molding, door jambs and heavier trim.
products.skip_if: You want smaller holes to fill; 16-gauge nails leave less to putty.

products.name: 3PLUS HT64SP 16 Gauge Pneumatic Straight Finish Nailer
products.verdict: The cheapest finish nailer here, with tool-free depth, a 360° exhaust, quick jam release and interchangeable triggers for single or bump fire.
products.best_for: A one-room trim job on a budget.
products.skip_if: You'll use it often; Metabo's 5-year warranty is worth the extra.

products.name: 3PLUS HDA1564SP 15 Gauge Angled Finish Nailer
products.verdict: A budget 15-gauge angled nailer for about half the Metabo's price, with tool-free depth, a no-mar tip and a 360° exhaust.
products.best_for: Crown and casing on a budget.
pros: About half the Metabo NT65MA4's price

products.name: HBT HBT64P 16 Gauge Finish Nailer with Magnesium Housing and Carrying Case
products.verdict: A magnesium-housed 16-gauge with a flip switch between bump and sequential fire, tool-free depth and jam release, a spare no-mar tip and a case, for under $60.
products.best_for: A budget 16-gauge with a real mode switch.
products.skip_if: You want a warranty term; none is listed.

products.name: BOSTITCH Finish Nailer Kit, 16GA, Smart Point, Pneumatic (BTFP71917)
products.verdict: A pro 16-gauge with Bostitch's Smart Point nose for accurate placement, oil-free operation that won't stain trim, Dial-A-Depth, and a 7-year warranty.
products.best_for: Painted or stained trim where oil spots matter.
products.skip_if: Budget matters; the Metabo NT65M2S is $40 less with a strong record.

products.name: DOTOOL Finish Nailer 16GA 1-inch to 2-1/2-inch Finish Nails Pneumatic Nail Gun (T64C)
products.verdict: A budget aluminum 16-gauge with tool-free depth and jam release and a 360° exhaust. The listing's claim that it handles subfloors, roof decking and sheathing is wrong for a 16-gauge finish nailer.
products.best_for: Occasional trim if the cheaper picks are out of stock.
products.skip_if: You need bump fire; only sequential is listed.
cons: Lists framing jobs a finish nailer can't do

products.name: meite T64A 16 Gauge Pneumatic Finish Nailer for 1-1/4 to 2-1/2 Inch Nails
products.verdict: A 3.86 lb aluminum 16-gauge with a quick-release nose for jams, tool-free depth and a 360° exhaust.
products.skip_if: You want a track record; it has 17 reviews.
cons: Firing modes and warranty not listed

products.name: DEWALT Finish Nailer with Precision Point, 16GA (DWFP71917)
products.verdict: DEWALT's 16-gauge Precision Point kit, rated 4.6 stars. The Amazon listing repeats the product name five times instead of listing specs, so check DEWALT's site for details.
products.skip_if: You want specs before buying; the listing has none.

products.name: BOSTITCH BTFP72156 Smart Point 15GA FN Style Angle Finish Nailer Kit
products.verdict: A pro 15-gauge kit with an integrated air blower to clear dust before you nail, a flip-out 16-inch on-center gauge for wall trim, Smart Point nose, Dial-A-Depth and a 7-year warranty.
products.best_for: Trim carpenters doing doors, jambs and crown all day.
products.skip_if: You trim one room; the Metabo NT65MA4 is $67 less.

avoid.name: NuMax Pneumatic 3-in-1 Nail Gun, 16 GA & 18 GA Finish Nailer, Brad Nailer, Stapler (SL31)
avoid.flag: 16-gauge nails only to 2 in; one gun for three fasteners
avoid.verdict: A do-everything gun that's short on the one thing a finish nailer is for. For about the same money, the 3PLUS HT64SP drives 16-gauge nails to 2-1/2 inches.
reasons: It only takes 16-gauge nails up to 2 inches. Dedicated finish nailers here drive 2-1/2-inch nails, the length you need to reach framing through casing and jambs.

One driver and magazine handle 16-gauge nails, 18-gauge brads and staples. The narrower brads and staples run in a channel sized for the thicker 16-gauge nail, a compromise no dedicated nailer has to make.
At 4.1 stars it's tied for the lowest rating here, with a 1-year warranty and 30 days on wear parts.

buyers_guide.a: 16-gauge nails are thinner and leave smaller holes, fine for baseboard, casing and most trim. 15-gauge nails are thicker and hold better in heavy crown, door jambs and hardwood, and angled 15-gauge magazines fit into corners.

Brad nailers shoot thin 18-gauge brads for light trim, small moldings and crafts. Finish nailers drive heavier 15 or 16-gauge nails up to 2-1/2 inches, long enough to hold casing and baseboard into the studs.

buyers_guide.q: What size compressor do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Finish nailers use little air. A small pancake or hot-dog compressor that holds 90 PSI keeps up with one nailer easily.

buyers_guide.q: What are DA and FN nails?
buyers_guide.a: Angled 15-gauge nailers use either DA (34°) or FN (25°) style nails, and they aren't interchangeable. Check which your nailer takes before buying nails.
Sequential fires one nail per trigger pull for precise placement. Bump fire shoots each time the nose is pressed while the trigger is held, which is faster on long runs. A switch lets you choose.
